name: Hadad
bio: Hadad was a member of Edom's royal family. When David's army, under Joab, spent six months in Edom killing every male there, Hadad escaped as a small child, fleeing with some of his father's officials through Midian and Paran to Egypt. Pharaoh received him warmly, giving him a house, land, and provisions, and eventually gave him his own wife's sister — sister of Queen Tahpenes — in marriage; she bore him a son, Genubath, who was raised in Pharaoh's own household alongside Pharaoh's sons. When Hadad later heard that David and Joab were both dead, he asked Pharaoh's permission to return to his own country; Pharaoh, puzzled at what Hadad could be lacking in Egypt, let him go anyway. The LORD raised up Hadad as an adversary against Solomon, late in his reign, as part of the judgment for Solomon's unfaithfulness (1 Kings 11:14-22, 25).
